name: Jerijah
title: Head of the Hebronites
summary: Jerijah (also known as Jerijah from Hebron) was a Levite of the Hebronite clan who served under King David. He was appointed head of the Hebronites and given responsibility for important administrative and religious tasks on both sides of the Jordan.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the Hebronites
keyEvents.description: In David's fortieth year as king, capable men were found among the Hebronites under the leadership of Jerijah in Jazer in Gilead.

keyEvents.title: Appointment as head of the Hebronites
keyEvents.description: Jerijah was identified as the head of the Hebronites according to their clans and families, and was placed in a prominent leadership position.

keyEvents.title: Administrative responsibility east of the Jordan
keyEvents.description: King David appointed Jerijah and his brothers, 2,700 capable men, over the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh to oversee all matters concerning God and the king.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the Hebronites under David
keyEvents.description: The Hebronites were mustered and registered in the fortieth year of David's reign, and Jerijah led a significant group responsible for religious and civil affairs.

keyEvents.title: Division of service among the Levites
keyEvents.description: As part of David's organization of the Levitical service, Jerijah and his relatives were counted as the first among the sons of Hebron and given specific duties.
